newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico agrees subsidised milk plan for poor - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico agrees subsidised milk plan for poor - paper.

text.p: Mexico's Trade Ministry has agreed with dairymen and milk industrialists to start a program of direct subsised milk sales to poor people in marginalized areas, the daily Reforma said Friday.
Israel Gutierrez, Deputy Trade Minister, told Reforma that 500,000 litres of milk per day will be sold to the poor at 3 pesos per litre from August 1.
Normal milk prices, now no longer controled by the government, are at least 25 percent higher in stores and supermarkets.

Gutierrez denied the move was not a form of electioneering before the key mid-term vote in July 6. He said the objective was to stimulate milk consumption and to promote a basic food product in remote parts of Mexico.
